question: Can a class-balanced, isotonic-calibrated gradient-boosting model give better-ranked and better-calibrated patient mortality risk than a k-means cluster-rate baseline on a public ICU-style dataset?
method: Stratified 75/25 split (seed 42); preprocessing fit on train only. Baseline: k-means on standardized features, k chosen by silhouette on train, test patients get the train death rate of their cluster. Improved: class-balanced LightGBM (hyperparameters by 5-fold CV on train), isotonic calibration fit on out-of-fold train predictions. Test set used once. Seeds 42/43/44; mean and std reported.

dataset.name: UCI Heart Failure Clinical Records (ICU-style stand-in)

metric_name: ROC-AUC on held-out test set (mean over seeds 42, 43, 44)
baseline: k-means cluster analysis on standardized features; test risk = training death rate of cluster (k by silhouette)
improved: class-balanced LightGBM (CV-tuned on train) with isotonic calibration fit on out-of-fold train predictions
notes: Stand-in dataset, not the paper's pneumonia ICU data; the paper's result is not reproduced here. Small sample, so test estimates are noisy. 'time' (follow-up duration) is excluded as post-outcome leakage. Dataset is small enough that no subsampling was needed. Hyperparameters were chosen by CV on train only with seed 42. Isotonic calibration uses out-of-fold predictions from 80% models, applied to the full-train model. Brier and balanced accuracy use the training prevalence as threshold. Test set used once.
